judgeScores.evidence: The concept directly serves content creators, matches the account's evidence-and-boundaries promise, separates optional heat from durable search/save value, and makes a distinct same-task decision promise.

The 72-second progression moves cleanly from unsupported verdict to evidence boundary, rubric, three proofs, transfer, and action; the actual result cells must still be filled only after the research gate.

Each shot has a cognitive and evidence function, transitions follow meaning changes, and neutral cards avoid rights dependence; the middle three table shots require disciplined typography to remain legible on a phone.
Title, cover, first frame, search query, save-oriented artifact, comment coding, series handoff, and current-rule gate are coherent; platform distribution remains correctly unclaimed.

A creator can quickly understand and save the three checks, while visible scope statements support trust; usefulness depends on the creator populating the promised same-task evidence rather than leaving the tables abstract.

The experiment isolates title, defines matching outcomes and a limited proxy, states minimum evidence and confounds, and has a decision rule; four non-random posts can inform the next iteration but cannot establish a general causal law.
